description: Annotated references for the reference-identity benchmark. Every raw_text is copied byte for byte from claimtrace/backend/uploads/parsed/*.references.json, including the PDF extractor's artifacts. acceptable_dois is filled in from --mode record, never guessed: see tests/benchmarks/recorded/. Cases carrying their own candidates are constructed, and their notes say so.

cases.raw_text: [1] Artem Babenko and Victor Lempitsky. The inverted multi-index. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 2014.

query.title: The inverted multi-index
query.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

expected.notes: the TPAMI article. The CVPR 2012 conference version is a different work with a different DOI and is banned. Both providers returned the TPAMI record, dated 2014 and 2015.

query.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30

expected.notes: CONSTRUCTED, from the recorded set for 92574678-58. The recorded set holds seven of these, and with that many the title never matches exactly once anyway. Reduced to one, a weighted rule scores the exact title plus the verbatim author list over any bar it would set, and reports the fabricated record as verified. This is the case the structural filters exist for, and a live query cannot produce it.

cases.raw_text: [30] Alireza Makhzani and Brendan Frey. K-sparse autoencoders. In International Conference on Representation Learning, 2014.

expected.notes: CONSTRUCTED, from the recorded set for f940bcbf-30. The preprint alone, so nothing else can carry the decision. Its venue is a repository and the reference names a conference, and its year is one before the reference's. If either the venue requirement or the year tolerance were a fraction tighter this correct record would be rejected.
